content: GOAL: orient in the workspace before proposing a metric. READ: glob of the agent directory (only running.json, session.jsonl, stderr.log, progress.jsonl, opencode.json). OBSERVED: no SID tables or reference arrays are copied into the agent directory; the parent research tree is the only place they could live. STILL OPEN: locating the exported SID tables and the Issue #126 frozen behaviour reference.

GOAL: deliver one in-scope hyperbolic metric. READ: agent dir and parent metric_round tree (no SID table readable in-session); contract; known baselines (Q_H L1 +0.634, L2 +0.287, L3 +0.393; bucket count -0.065). REASONED: within-bucket proximity metrics risk being judged a re-expression of same-bucket ratio, and level-1-only scores duplicate Q_H. So the metric never compares a prefix value against a score: it compares the ordering of pair distances implied by the whole code tree (LCA split depth, Poincare geodesic, curvature -1, edge tau=ln256, derived from the codebook) with the ordering of Lorentz geodesic distances (exp_0 lift, curvature -1) of the frozen reference, as ONE Spearman rho. Pairs from a deterministic stride on item id; no validation/test interaction; nothing tuned. DECISION: propose HTGO (hyperbolic tree geodesic ordering). STILL OPEN: no empirical rho on the 97 pairs possible (no table access); tie fraction and the h(i,j) in {0,L} degeneracy are the behaviours to watch.

ANSWER (final, complete):
METRIC: HTGO-hyperbolic-tree-geodesic-ordering
TITLE: Spearman agreement between Poincare-geodesic SID-tree distances and Lorentz distances of the frozen reference
FORMULA: N items; L levels; B=256 codes; K=-1. Item i has code path c_i=(c_i1..c_iL). Reference gives source-side x_i in R^d. LIFT xt_i=(sqrt(1+||x_i||^2), x_i); Lorentz product <u,v>_L=-u0v0+sum u_k v_k; dL(i,j)=arccosh(sqrt(1+||x_i||^2)*sqrt(1+||x_j||^2)-<x_i,x_j>). SID tree: h(i,j)=number of leading agreeing positions; tau=ln B; dT(i,j)=2*tau*(L-h(i,j)) (Poincare geodesic through the LCA in the ball of curvature -1, b-ary tree with edge length tau). Pair set deterministic: sort by item id, I={0,s,2s,...}, s=max(1,floor(N/2000)), n<=2000, all pairs i<j. METRIC = Spearman rank correlation (average ranks for ties) of {dT} vs {dL} over C(n,2) pairs, in [-1,1], higher better.
INPUTS: exported SID table [item_id, c_1..c_L]; frozen Issue #126 reference source-side x_i per item id. Nothing else; no training split, no val/test interaction, no recall.
GEOMETRY: (1) reference = hyperboloid model of H^d, curvature fixed K=-1, each item is exp_0(x_i)=(cosh||x_i||, sinh||x_i||*x_i/||x_i||), dL is the Lorentz geodesic distance. (2) SID side = Poincare ball of the same curvature -1, code tree embedded with edge length tau=ln256=5.545177 (node at depth k sits at radius tanh(k*tau/2)), dT the Poincare geodesic length via the LCA. (3) The metric compares two orderings of geodesic distances of the same kind; curvature is what makes far pairs additive (dL ~ ||x_i||+||x_j||) rather than quadratic, which is the only regime where a tree distance can agree with the reference at all. No scale, temperature or length fitted.
WHY IT TRACKS RECALL: Stage-3 walks a beam down the prefix tree, so recall@10 is high exactly when the tree's branching order matches the reference similarity order at the depths the beam traverses, not only at level 1. dT encodes the whole path (early split = large, late split = small, every level weighted equally). Over Q_H: Q_H scores prefix ranking at level 1 only and collapses at levels 2-3; HTGO never tests a prefix value against a score, only the relative split depth of pairs against curved reference distance, so deep-level degradation registers as lost rank signal instead of being hidden. It is also invariant to bucket sizes, so it is not bucket count or same-bucket ratio.
COMPUTE: n<=2000, ~2.0e6 pairs; one d-dim dot product plus an integer LCA test per pair (~1.3e8-5e8 flops for d=64-256) and two argsorts of 2e6 float64 for the ranks; single pass, no iteration, no factorisation: well under a minute on 24587 items / 256 codes.
RISKS: near-constant dL (tie-dominated Spearman) if reference vectors are near-collinear; global rank statistic weakly penalises a few misplaced hubs; very large ||x|| makes the hyperboloid lift norm-dominated (a property of the reference, reported not corrected); stride sample clustered if item-id order correlates with code order.
FAILURE MODE: worst on a SID table whose deeper levels are item identifiers, where h(i,j) is almost always 0 or L: dT takes only two values, its variance collapses, Spearman is near zero or undefined, and HTGO correctly reports that the tree carries only same-item/different-item information - exactly the level-2/level-3 regime, registered as failure rather than masked by a high same-bucket ratio.
END METRIC
